categoryCorrections.reason: Plain-language educational content about mortgages provided to customers at key milestones is the paid deliverable for a mortgage broker service, not internal customer support; it would otherwise mistag as cmo if treated as internal content marketing.

Tracking referral sources and their conversion quality is internal business intelligence/vendor management, not business development; drafting thank-you messages is a minor component and doesn't make the core task sales-focused (sales owns finding/closing NEW customers, not managing existing referral logistics).

customization.notes: Core delivery tasks replaced with mortgage-specific application packaging and deal tracking; BCFSA licence monitoring and FINTRAC KYC checker added as locked compliance tasks; referral tracker added since referrals are the sole channel; generic social posting removed as it doesn't fit a referral-only brokerage at MVP-0; lead scoring and outreach dialed back to weekly to match lower volume of first-time buyer referrals.

charterDraft.sharpenedIdea: A lean mortgage brokerage that guides first-time homebuyers through pre-approval and closing by automating paperwork, compliance, and client education.
charterDraft.mvpDefinition: Launch by handling pre-approval and application assembly for first-time buyers in your region. Start with 5–10 clients per month, focusing on sourcing leads from referral partners and real-estate networks, preparing clean mortgage application packages for major lenders (TD, RBC, Scotiabank), and sending educational milestone updates so borrowers understand each step. No investor loans, no commercial deals — pure first-time buyer flow.

tasks: Draft a rolling weekly plan each Monday highlighting who owns which client deals and any upcoming milestone deadlines.
Flag any cross-team conflicts — for example, if a borrower needs docs from Delivery but Support is waiting on their reply — and surface them to the founder for quick resolution.
Create and send invoices to clients for retainer fees or per-application fees matched to your pricing structure.
Tag and categorize all business expenses (software, lender partner fees, tech tools) and flag any unusual spending.
Project cash flow for the next 30, 60, and 90 days based on expected client flow and deal closures; alert if runway drops below 3 months.
Track all tax deadlines (GST filings, corporate tax, payroll remittance) and prepare a summary packet for your accountant each quarter.
Review all client contracts and lender agreements for legal red flags and flag expiring service agreements or regulatory deadlines.
Monitor your BCFSA mortgage broker licence for any expiring education credits, insurance requirements, or renewal notices; ensure all documentation stays current.
Verify that every new borrower file has complete FINTRAC identification (name, DOB, address, ID type) and anti-money-laundering KYC records; flag any incomplete files before they go to lenders.
Spot-check each completed client work — application packages, educational documents, deal status updates — before they're sent out; catch missing forms or errors.

Assemble every borrower's mortgage application package by collecting and organizing income verification, employment letters, credit check consents, property appraisals, and any other lender requirements.
Track each client's deal status as it moves through lenders (submitted, conditionally approved, additional docs requested, funded) and send plain-language status updates to keep them informed.

Write and send clear, jargon-free explainers to first-time buyers at key moments — explaining mortgage types, interest rates, the approval timeline, what to expect at closing — so they feel confident and informed.
Score and qualify every inbound lead (referral, website inquiry, event) by assessing their likelihood to close and enriching their profile with publicly available info.
Draft personalized first outreach emails and follow-up sequences for qualified leads to book an initial consultation.
Log all client interactions in your CRM, update deal stages as they progress, and flag leads that have gone quiet so they don't fall through the cracks.
Build custom mortgage quotes and pre-approval proposals using your rate templates and the borrower's financial profile to send during the initial consultation.
Draft welcome sequences for newly signed clients including a onboarding checklist, document requirements, and a 'getting started' timeline so they know what comes next.
Read all incoming client messages, tag them by urgency (e.g., document request, rate question, closing question), and draft helpful replies to common questions without escalation.
Spot complex or frustrated client messages and escalate them to the founder with full context — previous deal history, outstanding issues, sentiment — so they can respond personally.
Manage your calendar and send booking confirmations and reminder messages for all client consultation calls.

Track which referral sources (real-estate agents, previous clients, community partners) are sending you the best-quality leads; draft thank-you messages to keep those relationships warm and log source performance monthly.

monthOneGoals: Land and onboard 3–5 qualified first-time buyer clients for pre-approval and complete their application packages for lender submission.
Set up your BCFSA compliance infrastructure: confirm broker licence documents are filed, establish FINTRAC/KYC process, and document all check points in writing.
Build and test your application template and educational content so every client gets consistent, clear communications at each deal stage.
Establish 2–3 referral relationships (real-estate agents, financial advisors, community orgs) and send initial outreach to warm leads.
